cues.en: The declarative programming languages have several advantages over traditional languages. For example, programs in such languages are considerably shorter than equivalent programs in imperative languages. Here, for example, is a program in C, and here is the equivalent program in Erlang. Hello. Hello, Joe. Hello, Mike. Question. Does anyone care about the differences between declarative and imperative languages anymore? Don't be silly.
cues.zh: 声明式编程语言相比传统语言有几个优势。例如，用这种语言写的程序要比命令式语言的等价程序简短得多。比如，这里是一段 C 语言程序，而这里是用 Erlang 写的等价程序。你好。你好，Joe。你好，Mike。问个问题：现在还有人在乎声明式和命令式语言的区别吗？别傻了。

cues.en: The declarative imperative debate is always a crowd-pleaser. From what I can tell, kids these days are going with what's cool, like Node.js and Ruby on Rails. Let's ask Robert. Hello, Robert. Hello, Mike. Joe's back to talking about declarative languages again. I just think Erlang's got a problem when its spokesman is an old fuddy-duddy. Eh, Joe? Bite me. Robert, what do you think? Erlang's the schezer, but I can't blame kids for picking something a little less.
cues.zh: 声明式与命令式的争论向来喜闻乐见。据我所知，现在的年轻人只看什么最酷，比如 Node.js 和 Ruby on Rails。我们来问问 Robert。你好，Robert。你好，Mike。Joe 又在念叨声明式语言了。我觉得如果代言人是个老古董，Erlang 就有麻烦了。对吧，Joe？滚一边去。Robert，你怎么看？Erlang 确实牛，但我也理解年轻人为什么选没那么……

cues.en: Krusty. Erlang's image is stuck in the 1980s. It's the banana rammer of languages. Okay. Tell you what. This is bullshit. If kids these days don't want to use Erlang, which is the real rockstar tech, then fuck it. I'll turn this video off and go home. Take my nine nines with me. Joe. I didn't mean anything by it. Yeah, Joe. Mike was just trying to be constructive. Joe, turn the video back on. I won't.
cues.zh: 过时的东西。Erlang 的形象还停留在 80 年代。它是编程语言里的 Bananarama。行吧。听我说。这简直是扯淡。如果现在的年轻人不想用 Erlang 这种真正的摇滚巨星级技术，那就拉倒。我关掉视频回家了。带上我的 9 个 9 撤退。Joe。我没别的意思。对啊，Joe。Mike 只是想提点建设性意见。Joe，把视频重新打开。才不。

cues.en: I won't have heard I'm disparaged. Yo, yo, yo. I can totally help you geysers. Who said that? All Erlang needs is an image upgrade. That's very interesting. Lots of things from the 80s are cool. Just look at Fraggle Rock and Super Mario Brothers. What the hell is that? It's one of those Ruby hipsters. Watch it, Grandpa. Just because I carry my Mac in a messenger bag and have great taste in those rings doesn't mean I use Ruby. I for one am interested in what the little girl has to say. Yo, whatever.
cues.zh: 我绝容不得它被贬低。哟哟哟，老头们，我绝对能帮你们。谁在说话？Erlang 只需要来一次形象升级。这很有意思。80 年代有很多很酷的东西啊。看看《Fraggle Rock》和《超级马里奥兄弟》就知道了。这特么是个啥？是个玩 Ruby 的文青。小心点，老头。我背着邮差包装 Mac、鼻环品味绝佳，可不代表我用 Ruby。我倒是挺想听听这个小姑娘要说什么。切，随便吧。

cues.en: First, we have to fix the name. A language named after a 19th century Danish mathematician is about as cool as having a Facebook account. It's just like the olden days. When Erlang was banned, we had to change the name. That's right. When Erlang fell out of fashion at Ericsson, we changed the name to OTP. Three of the trendiest names we could think of. Open. Telecom. Platform. Gives me the chills just thinking about it. Okay.
cues.zh: 首先，我们得改掉这个名字。用 19 世纪丹麦数学家命名的语言，就像现在还玩 Facebook 一样老土。跟当年简直一模一样。当年 Erlang 被禁时，我们不得不改名。没错。当 Erlang 在 Ericsson 失宠时，我们把名字改成了 OTP。我们能想到的三个最潮的词。Open。Telecom。Platform。想想都起鸡皮疙瘩。行了。

cues.en: That's bullcrap. No one cares about telecom platforms. We need something fresh. Something edgy. Like Erlang on Rails. Jesus Christ. The last thing you want to do is imitate. No, something original. How about Erlang++? I got it. We keep OTP, but with a hip, edgy twist. Check it. Your language will hereby be known as... Outlaw. Techno. Psycho Bitch. It does spell OTP. Don't know what it has to do with software.
cues.zh: 纯属扯淡。没人关心什么电信平台。我们需要新鲜的东西。带点棱角。比如 Erlang on Rails。天呐。你最不该做的就是模仿。不，得来点原创的。Erlang++ 怎么样？我有主意了。保留 OTP，但融入时髦又叛逆的元素。听好了。你们这门语言从此将被称为……Outlaw。Techno。Psycho Bitch。首字母确实是 OTP。就是不知道跟软件有半毛钱关系。

cues.en: What do you think, Joe? I absolutely love it. That name is fucking gangster. Yeah, Joe. You rule. Okay, next thing we need is a video that is just as cool as the original Erlang the movie, but speaks to today's programmer hipster. I'm thinking something like this. Yo, what up, bitches? Rex here. This time I'm talking about a badass new language called Outlaw techno psycho bitch, or OTP for short. So, you all know I'm a huge Ruby fan.
cues.zh: Joe，你觉得呢？我他妈太爱了。这名字真他妈屌。对，Joe，你最牛。好，接下来我们需要一个视频，和原版 Erlang the movie 一样酷，但要能对上今天程序员潮人的胃口。我想的是这样。哟，婊子们，最近咋样？我是 Rex。这次我要聊一个屌炸天的新语言，叫 Outlaw techno psycho bitch，简称 OTP。你们都知道，我是 Ruby 的超级粉丝。

cues.en: Ruby gives you 15 ways to do the same thing, and freedom of choice is good. Then I realized that's just 15 different ways to create really slow, crappy programs. Then I started using Node.js. I like Node because, as my hero Ryan Dahl says, it's like coloring with crayons and playing with Duplo blocks. But as it turns out, it's less like playing with Duplo blocks, and more like playing with slinkies. Slinkies that get tangled together and impossible to separate. So then I checked out Blotekno Psycho Bitch.
cues.zh: Ruby 给你 15 种方式做同一件事，选择自由是好事。后来我意识到，那只是 15 种做出超慢、超烂程序的不同方式。然后我开始用 Node.js。我喜欢 Node，因为我的英雄 Ryan Dahl 说，它就像用蜡笔涂色、玩 Duplo 积木。但事实证明，它不太像玩 Duplo 积木，更像玩 Slinkies。还是那种缠在一起、根本解不开的 Slinkies。所以后来我去看了 Blotekno Psycho Bitch。

cues.en: It's a language out of Sweden that can be used to build web-scale, asynchronous, non-blocking, charted, event-driven, message-passing, no sequel, reliable, highly available, high-performance, real-time, clusterable, badass, rockstar. Get the girls. Get the boys. Impress your mom. Impress your cat. Applications. Try and all. Like Hero says, we should not be supporting more programming languages. That we should be killing them. That all these bullshit projects are confusing people.
cues.zh: 这是一种来自瑞典的语言，能用来构建 Web 规模、异步、非阻塞、图表化、事件驱动、消息传递、no sequel、可靠、高可用、高性能、实时、可集群、屌炸天、摇滚明星级的……吸引女孩。吸引男孩。惊艳你妈。惊艳你的猫。应用。都来试试吧。就像 Hero 说的，我们不该支持更多编程语言，应该把它们干掉。这些狗屁项目只会把人搞晕。

cues.en: But, Psycho Bitch is just so damn cool, I couldn't resist giving it a try. The first thing Psycho Bitch kills off, is curly braces. Thank God. After a half century of curly braces, we need something that's fresh. Psycho Bitch uses single character block delimiters, like in sentences. My hero Ryan Dolph says, math is not necessary, that people who think it's superior to curly braces are wrong. But, I figure, if math can get a rover to Mars, maybe it can help us write better programs.
cues.zh: 但 Psycho Bitch 实在太他妈酷了，我忍不住试了一把。Psycho Bitch 第一个干掉的就是花括号。谢天谢地。花括号用了半个世纪，我们需要点新鲜东西。Psycho Bitch 用单字符块分隔符，就像句子里的标点。我的英雄 Ryan Dolph 说，数学没必要，认为数学比花括号更优越的人是错的。但我想，如果数学能把漫游车送上火星，也许它也能帮我们写出更好的程序。

cues.en: Psycho Bitch gets pretty uptight about logic. If you say that X is 1, and then turn around, and say X is 2, Psycho Bitch goes ape shit. She's like, what the hell? When did 1 start equaling 2? Psycho Bitch has this great feature called pattern matching. You define the patterns, and if there's a match, your program keeps going. If something doesn't match, it crashes. Like assertions, but built in. What happens when your program crashes? Psycho Bitch has you covered. It monitors your code.
cues.zh: Psycho Bitch 对逻辑非常较真。你说 X 是 1，转头又说 X 是 2，她就炸毛了。她会想，搞什么鬼？1 什么时候开始等于 2 了？Psycho Bitch 有个超棒的特性叫模式匹配。你定义模式，如果匹配，程序就继续跑。如果有东西不匹配，程序就崩溃。像断言，但它是内置的。程序崩溃了怎么办？Psycho Bitch 帮你兜底。它会监控你的代码。

cues.en: and restarts things that break. It's like the Terminator. You can blast it in the face with a shotgun. It stops for a second. Then keeps on coming. I've written a chat server in Psycho Bitch. It's where all my friends and me can't chat about how awesome Ryan Dahl is. Because the server is written in Psycho Bitch, it can easily handle thousands of concurrent users. Shit, did I say thousands? Because I meant tens of thousands. And by tens of thousands, I mean hundreds of thousands.
cues.zh: 并重启坏掉的东西。它就像终结者。你可以用霰弹枪轰它的脸。它停一下，然后继续冲上来。我用 Psycho Bitch 写了一个聊天服务器。我和所有朋友就在那里聊 Ryan Dahl 有多牛。因为这个服务器是用 Psycho Bitch 写的，轻松扛住数千并发用户。靠，我说数千？我是说数万。说数万，其实是数十万。

cues.en: I'm already logged in as myself, at the top. I'll log in as another user. You say something using the tell command. The messages are received instantly, even though there are hundreds of thousands of connected users. I'll use the yell command to broadcast a message to every user. That literally sent the message to 300,000 users, about a second. Okay, 300,000 concurrent users is impressive. But even Node.js can do that. Let's try something hard.
cues.zh: 最上方我已经登录了自己的账号。我现在用另一个用户登录。你用 tell 命令说了些话。虽然有数十万在线用户，但消息瞬间就收到了。我用 yell 命令向所有用户广播一条消息。这真的一秒左右就发送给了30万名用户。好吧，30万并发用户确实很厉害。但就算是 Node.js 也能做到。我们来点有难度的。

cues.en: To make things interesting, we'll trigger a bug on the server. Damn, I must have said something bad. But as you can see, Mary and Jack can still chat. Of the 300,000 users on the server, I'm the only one affected. Let's see if we can fix the bug. Here's the code. Holy crap. It looks like the original programmer, in his zeal, added some forbidden utterances. Let's clean this up, because we don't want to censor. Okay. I recompiled the code. Next, I'll reload it.
cues.zh: 为了增加点趣味，我们在服务器上触发一个 bug。糟糕，我肯定是说了什么不该说的话。但大家可以看到，Mary 和 Jack 依然可以聊天。在服务器上的30万用户里，我是唯一受影响的。我们来看看能不能修复这个 bug。这是代码。天呐。看来原作者当年热情过头，加了些违禁词。我们把它清理干净，因为我们不想搞言论审查。好的。我重新编译了代码。接下来，我要热重载它。

cues.en: in real time, with 300,000 concurrent chats going on. Done. In case you missed it, here it is again, in slow motion. For some of you, what you just saw, is not self-explanatory, if gracefully handling bugs, with hundreds of thousands of concurrent sessions, and fixing them in real time without stopping the server seems passé. You can always use Ruby, then, when your app doesn't scale, move to Node.js, then, when you can't maintain your code because it's a pile of tangled slinkies, move to PsychoBitch.
cues.zh: 在30万个并发聊天进行的同时，实时重载。搞定。要是你刚才错过了，这里放慢动作再演示一遍。对你们中的有些人来说，刚才看到的一切可能并不直观，如果在几十万并发会话中优雅地处理 bug，并且不用停机就能实时修复看起来已经过时的话。你大可以去用 Ruby，等应用无法扩展时再转向 Node.js，最后，当你的代码乱成一团麻无法维护时，再投奔 PsychoBitch。

cues.en: With that experience, you can appreciate what you just saw, for the rest of you. Yes, that just happened. So, what do you guys think about Psycho Bitch? She's utterly terrifying. It makes me wonder if perhaps Psycho Bitch is a real person. You mean, is the name based on my experience with a girlfriend who's batshit crazy, drop dead gorgeous, brilliant, and brags to her friends about costing me tens of thousands of dollars in therapy over the last three years? Oh shit, I know a girl like that. She scarred me, for life.
cues.zh: 有了那样的切身体会，你才能真正领略刚才那一幕的威力，至于其他人。没错，刚才那一幕真的发生了。那么，大家觉得 Psycho Bitch 怎么样？她简直可怕极了。这不禁让我好奇，Psycho Bitch 会不会真有其人？你是说，这个名字是不是源自我的某位前女友——她疯得离谱、美得惊人、聪明绝顶，还向朋友炫耀过去三年花了我好几万美元看心理医生？卧槽，我还真认识一个这样的女孩。她给我留下了终生阴影。

cues.en: Literally. Seriously, I'll show you the scars.
cues.zh: 真的。说认真的，我给你看伤疤。
